title: Prosciutto e Melone
author: Marco Bellini
desc: The classic Italian summer antipasto, thin slices of delicate prosciutto crudo draped over ripe, sweet cantaloupe -- a study in contrast between salty cured meat and juicy fruit.
longDesc: This effortless pairing depends entirely on the quality of its two ingredients: a genuinely ripe, fragrant melon and thinly sliced, high-quality prosciutto crudo, their opposing flavors, sweet and salty, balancing each other perfectly.
ingredients: 150 g (5.3 oz) prosciutto crudo, thinly sliced
steps: Halve the melon and remove the seeds.
Cut into wedges, or use a melon baller to scoop rounds, and remove the rind if using wedges.
Arrange the melon on a serving platter.
Drape each piece with a thin slice of prosciutto, or wrap the melon pieces if using rounds.
Finish with a crack of black pepper and a few torn mint leaves if using.
chefTips: A genuinely ripe, fragrant melon makes all the difference -- smell the stem end, which should be sweetly aromatic.
Use a thinly sliced, good-quality prosciutto, as its delicate flavor is easily lost if sliced too thick.
Serve well chilled, as this dish is meant to be a refreshing warm-weather starter.
commonMistakes: Using an underripe or bland melon, which this simple dish depends on entirely.
Using thickly sliced prosciutto, which overwhelms rather than complements the melon.
Serving at room temperature rather than properly chilled.
servedWith: A chilled Prosecco or light white wine
healthBenefits: Melon provides vitamin C and hydration; prosciutto contributes protein.
culturalNote: Prosciutto e melone is a beloved fixture of Italian summer antipasto spreads, its simple sweet-salty pairing found on trattoria menus throughout the country.
